description: libuv's loop that picks the next callback to run on the single JavaScript thread, phase by phase, while work remains.
timers (`setTimeout`/`setInterval`) → pending callbacks → poll (I/O) → check (`setImmediate`) → close callbacks.
Promise reactions, code after `await` and `queueMicrotask`. Drained after every callback, before the loop moves on.
Node-only queue drained before the promise microtasks. Recursive use can starve I/O.
Runs in the check phase, right after poll. Inside an I/O callback it always fires before `setTimeout(fn, 0)`.
Synchronous CPU work keeps the thread busy, so timers, I/O callbacks and every other request wait.
libuv's worker threads (4 by default) for file system, DNS lookup, crypto and zlib work. Results return through the poll phase.
